_comment: Scenario-staged routing demo beside impassable terrain: a brittle player cavalry unit (60 mounts at morale 0.5) starts just west of the default hill (Rect2(1150, 380, 250, 200)) and holds there until an enemy cavalry charge from its WESTERN flank comes in. Both units stand clear of the hill for the whole clip: the router's block is 280 wu wide, so its centre at x=960 keeps its eastern file 50 wu clear of the hill's west face. The pursuer's target sits 190 wu west of the hill and 40 wu below its bottom edge, so its leg is clear of the hill and it charges straight east. Measured with a 2-tick dense state dump: the router holds at its spawn through tick 120, the charge makes contact at tick 159 and drives the router back about 60 wu west, the two fight one unbroken melee, and the router routs at tick 344. While the pursuer is still on it the router is held near where it broke (about (908, 661) at tick 440); once clear it flees north along the hill's west side (about (933, 605) at tick 560, (907, 220) at tick 680), every man clear of the hill, and rallies at tick 704 (ROUTING at 703, IDLE at 704) at about (906, 148), inside the clip (it ends at tick 720). It rallies at its full 221 wu/s flight, so it then pulls up with its men in step (anchor about (906, 129) at tick 710, still coasting at about (905, 99) when the clip ends); its men arrive at the rally already scrambled off their own slots by the interleaved fight (#1725). The pursuer's facing turns smoothly through the charge, with no snap larger than 20 degrees between 2-tick samples. This scenario does NOT show a rout detouring around the hill: the router's flight never meets it. The 'stands and fights when genuinely trapped' case is covered by test_trapped_routing_unit_fights_instead_of_fleeing. No player input needed; the scenario + seed make the clash deterministic. After the rout the pursuer's own deep column deforms: a 2-tick scan from the divergence (tick 343) reads a sustained shape residual of 142.2 wu against a 30 wu threshold, against 43.4 wu on the pre-#1739 merge-base; at this head the pursuer re-engages the router at tick 548 and swings round towards the south-east. Before the charge came straight in (rout at tick 469), the same scan from the rout read 75.4 wu: the straight charge did not cause the deformation. Because of it the declared checks pin the router's story beats with sparse post-rout samples (400, 560, 680, the rally at 703/704, and 710) rather than sampling the gallop densely. The pursuer's deformation, and the router's own scramble (judged only on the 16 ticks after its rally), are declared below as exemptions rather than sampled around.

shape_residual.reason: uid 1 (the pursuer): its own 80-mount deep column deforms after the rout. No #1739 code path runs in the pursuer's own update. #1739 reaches it only through the router: the router's full-pace flight, its decaying engaged latch and its refreshed enemy-contact flag; the latter two feed this unit's own _separate() pair test against the router (Unit.gd:5181) while the two are in contact. Meanwhile the router now gets away at its real pace: at tick 548 the pursuer, still on its ATTACK order against uid 0, re-engages it from a new angle, its facing swings from 59 to -117 degrees between ticks 544 and 568, and its anchor then backs away to the south-east to about (1115, 829) by tick 720. On the merge-base the pursuer trails the crawling router steadily with no swing. Sustained shape residual on a 2-tick scan from tick 343: 142.2 wu at this head against 43.4 wu on the merge-base (threshold 30). Tracked as a pursuer deforming on engaging a full-pace router in #1757, and by this clip's re-authoring in #1725. uid 0 (the router): it rallies at tick 704, and the 16 ticks to the clip's end are its only judged samples (a router is not judged). Its men reach the rally already far off their own slots: at tick 704 they stand 297 wu from their own slot on average (index-aligned) and 29.5 wu from the nearest slot, after the fight that starts with the two blocks interleaved. It then pulls up from its 221 wu/s flight (anchor y 147.5 at tick 704, 98.7 at tick 720) with its men in step, and the scramble carries over: sustained shape residual 236.8 wu on 2-tick samples, against 227.2 wu on main 1f4a77eb, where the anchor stopped dead on the rally. So the residual is the scramble, not the post-rally stop. Tracked by this clip's re-authoring in #1725.

overlap.reason: uid 0 (the router), judged only on the 16 ticks after its rally at tick 704: closest body pair 2.758 wu on 2-tick samples against the 5.0 wu floor, and 2.408 wu on main 1f4a77eb, where the anchor stopped dead on the rally. Its men reach the rally scrambled off their own slots (see the shape_residual reason), so the close pair is the scramble rather than the post-rally stop; the cause was not traced further. Tracked by this clip's re-authoring in #1725.
